procedure: Sourced /Users/vincenzo/esp/esp-idf-v5.5.4/export.sh in the same shell used for the acceptance run.
Ran make IDF_PORT=/dev/cu.usbmodem1101 IDF_ACCEPTANCE_MANUAL=passed IDF_FIRMWARE_REVISION=3a67803 idf-acceptance-report from nSealr/esp32 revision de58cb4.
The acceptance target detected the attached board and ESP-IDF/esptool availability before protocol exchange.
The target ran capability smoke, review-scenario smoke, a read-only security-fuse audit, a non-destructive post-audit hard reset, and a post-reset protocol recovery smoke.

Manual display/button observation had already passed for show-review, show-tags, show-long-content, show-scroll-review, show-dense-tags, show-unicode-review, show-control-escapes, show-request-error, button-approve, and button-reject.
expected_result: The flashed T-Display S3 firmware should remain a development-only USB/display signer scaffold: protocol smokes pass, trusted-review scenarios remain inspectable, post-fuse reset recovers the app protocol, and every real sign_event still returns signing_disabled.
observed_result: The acceptance report passed. Board detection found /dev/cu.usbmodem1101, native USB/JTAG serial, idf.py at /Users/vincenzo/esp/esp-idf-v5.5.4/tools/idf.py, and esptool.py at /Users/vincenzo/.espressif/python_env/idf5.5_py3.9_env/bin/esptool.py. Capability smoke verified 40 exchanges with 9 response frames and 31 expected rejection frames. Review-scenario smoke verified 9 exchanges covering 8 review scenarios with signing_disabled responses or expected rejection. The read-only fuse audit kept secure_boot, flash_encryption, debug_lock, download_mode, and manual_flash_encryption_download as production blockers. The post-fuse-audit protocol recovery smoke verified another 40 exchanges after hard reset. production_signing_ready remained false and runtime_signing_disabled remained a blocker.
limitations: This is development acceptance evidence for the current T-Display S3 USB/display signer scaffold, not production hardware-wallet certification.
The run did not enable secure boot, flash encryption, debug locking, persistent-secret storage, key provisioning, source public-key proof, companion signed-output verification, or real signing.
The flashed firmware revision was 3a67803; acceptance-report tooling was run from nSealr/esp32 revision de58cb4.
Manual observation status depends on human inspection of the physical display and onboard buttons; the JSON report records that status but does not replace production trusted-display acceptance.
The board is a no-camera T-Display S3 USB/display target and does not validate ESP32 QR-vault camera hardware.
